candidates.api_shape: movements shelf; first kits band_brake, expanding_shoe_brake, parking_pawl
candidates.fdm: Band, shoe, park pawl all print. Working friction is PLA-on-PLA or a bought liner.
candidates.name: brakes
candidates.why: Shaft-to-ground. Winch hold, hoist, park. Clutches join two shafts and the current blurb does not mention grounding. Three high-fit kits already named. The cleanest split on the prompt list.

candidates.api_shape: movements shelf; move escapement here; add lever, verge, gravity, going_barrel, geneva_stop
candidates.fdm: Two-plate escapements already print and animate. Going barrel is teeth + click on an existing spring.
candidates.name: clockwork
candidates.why: Feedback oscillator, not intermittent motion. Indexing is crank-in/steps-out (Geneva). Clockwork locks and impulses a resonator. escapement is misfiled today. Five-plus yes kits.

candidates.api_shape: movements shelf; Negator, remontoire, constant_force_compliant, gravity arm
candidates.fdm: Drums print, tape is bought steel or TPU demo. Compliant CF cells print flat.
candidates.name: constant_force
candidates.why: Flat F or T is a machinery class, not a spring (force rises with x) and not a screw. Cross-cuts three existing shelves, which is why agents miss it. Four named kits.

candidates.api_shape: movements shelf or a linkages subgroup; Klann, Jansen, walking-beam
candidates.fdm: Flat bars, published lengths, one rotary input. One leg is a semi-primitive; a chassis is a product.
candidates.name: leg_mechanisms
candidates.why: Walking is a distinct agent job. four_bar's usecase currently claims walking-robot legs. Search cannot hit Klann if it lives as an anonymous 6-bar. Rank below brakes/clockwork because the kits can also live under linkages if we refuse a 31st shelf.

candidates.api_shape: movements shelf; Bennett, spherical_four_bar, five_bar, delta_parallelogram, ups_strut
candidates.fdm: Bars and spherical pairs print. Axis concurrency is the pain, same as a Hooke joint.
candidates.name: spatial
candidates.why: Not planar and not a robot product. joints currently dumps wrists onto ball_socket and gimbal. A shelf keeps Delta/Stewart products out while naming the cells. Same rank logic as legs: useful, but linkages can absorb the kits.

candidates.fdm: A piston with an orifice, or a rotary vane in a viscous pot. Fluid is bought silicone. Envelope is printable. Eddy/magnetic dampers are hardware.
candidates.name: dampers
candidates.why: Energy dissipation is a real class (Norton, vehicle suspensions, door closers). Prompt listed it. Thinner than brakes: only two honest FDM kits. Add the shelf when the first kit lands, not before.

candidates.api_shape: elements shelf only if lip_seal / piston_ring / wiper ship as solids
candidates.fdm: Current seals are cutters. Lip/piston/wiper would be parts.
candidates.name: seals_elements
candidates.why: A shelf for three cutters is noise. Promote only after contact-seal solids exist.

candidates.api_shape: grow pulleys (sheave, tackle, cleat, capstan) rather than split
candidates.name: cable_tendon
candidates.why: Pulleys blurb already claims cable. Splitting now orphans grooved_drum. Revisit if tackle grows past six APIs.

candidates.fdm: Four miters print. The axle is a product.
candidates.name: differentials_shelf
candidates.why: One teaching kit. Not a class. Torsen/LSD/locked diffs are products.

candidates.fdm: A full Delta or Stewart is a finished machine.
candidates.name: parallel_robots
candidates.why: The prompt listed it. The cells are spatial/linkage primitives. The aisle would fill with products. Do not add.

candidates.name: magnetic_drives
candidates.why: Rejected on gears, clutches, couplings, bearings, linear. Not a printable working surface.

candidates.fdm: One variable-pitch V-pulley. Toroidal/ball CVTs are metal.
candidates.name: traction_cvt_shelf
candidates.why: One kit under pulleys. Not a shelf.

candidates.name: end_effectors_split
candidates.why: grippers already is the holding shelf. Splitting EOAT from clamps is taxonomy theater.

candidates.name: tooling_atc
candidates.why: Dock is the locate primitive. A tooling aisle would be finished ATC products.

candidates.name: heat
candidates.why: Prompt said heat? (out). Correct. Not a mechanism class this library should name.

rejected.name: springs_split
rejected.why: flexures already includes coil/leaf/wave/spiral. A 31st shelf to split energy from joints does not earn its keep.

rejected.name: pairs_shelf
rejected.why: joints is the pair shelf. Grow it with revolute_pair / cylindrical_pair / rod_end rather than adding 'pairs'.

summary:
A gallery shelf is justified when (1) it is a real machinery class agents search by name, (2) at least three FDM-printable semi-primitives would live there, and (3) those parts are currently misfiled or unshelved. Live CATEGORIES has 30 shelves: movements cover cams, chains, clutches, couplings, drives, flexures, fluid, gears, grippers, guides, indexing, joints, linear, linkages, pulleys, ratchets; elements cover bearings, closures, fasteners, fixtures, mechanisms; blocks cover cutters, lattices, meshutil, packing, patterns, prim, stepio, sweep, text. Overnight slices already proposed brakes, clockwork, constant_force, leg_mechanisms, and spatial. This slice ranks those against the prompt list and against classes nobody named.

What is already a shelf under another name. End-effectors are grippers. Cable/tendon is pulleys (blurb already says belt and cable) plus drag_chain. Differentials are one kit (bevel_differential) under gears, not a gearbox aisle. ATC is repeatable_dock under fixtures. Springs live inside flexures. Seals live as cutters (oring, labyrinth, gasket). Traction/CVT is one variable-pitch pulley under pulleys. Parallel robots are kits under linkages/spatial, not a robot aisle.

What should become a shelf. brakes: shaft-to-ground, opposite of clutches (shaft-to-shaft); band, expanding-shoe, parking-pawl, disc-pad are real and printable; clutches blurb is 'torque limiting and freewheeling' and has no ground. clockwork: a feedback oscillator (escapement + resonator + going barrel), not indexing (crank in, steps out); escapement is currently misfiled under indexing. constant_force: Negator, remontoire, compliant CF cell, gravity arm; they source a flat F or T, they are not screws or springs. leg_mechanisms: one-leg kits (Klann, Jansen, walking-beam) are a distinct agent job from four_bar; four_bar's usecase currently dumps walking-robot legs onto a crank-rocker. spatial: Bennett, spherical 4-bar, 5-bar, delta forearm, UPS strut; not planar linkages and not a finished robot. dampers: orifice dashpot and rotary vane damper are printable envelopes; viscous/eddy hardware stays out; thinner than brakes but a real class.

What must not become a shelf. Magnetic drives, magnetic bearings, magnetic gears: printed cages around bought magnets, rejected on every slice. Heat, thermoelectric, Stirling: out of scope. Finished parallel robots (Delta, Stewart, Agile Eye): products; the cells belong on spatial/linkages. Tooling/ATC products. A springs split from flexures: not enough confusion to pay for a 31st shelf. A seals elements shelf: only if lip/piston/wiper land as solids rather than cutters.
